question: A salesman offers a discount scheme of 'Buy 25 and get 5 free' on the purchase of notebooks in his shop. He professes that a notebook costs him ₹10, but in reality, it costs him ₹5. Find the difference between his profit percentage and scheme discount.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total CP for 30 notebooks (25 paid + 5 free) = 30 × ₹5 = ₹150

Total SP for 25 notebooks charged = 25 × ₹10 = ₹250

Profit % = [(250 − 150) ÷ 150] × 100 = 200/3 %

Discount % = [Free items ÷ Total items] × 100 = (5 ÷ 30) × 100 = 50/3 %

Difference = 200/3 % − 50/3 % = 150/3 % = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Scheme = Buy 25 get 5 free

Professed cost per notebook (Selling Price) = ₹10

Real cost per notebook (Cost Price) = ₹5

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = (Free Quantity ÷ Total Quantity) × 100

Profit % = (Total Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

 Total CP = 30 × ₹5 = ₹150
 
 Profit = ₹100 | Discount = 5 out of 30

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total items given to the customer = 25 + 5 = 30 items

⇒ Discount % = (5 ÷ 30) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 6) × 100 = 50/3 %

⇒ Total CP of 30 notebooks = 30 × ₹5 = ₹150

⇒ Total SP of 25 notebooks = 25 × ₹10 = ₹250

⇒ Total Profit = Total SP − Total CP = 250 − 150 = ₹100

⇒ Profit % = (100 ÷ 150) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (2 ÷ 3) × 100 = 200/3 %

⇒ Difference = Profit % − Discount %

⇒ Difference = 200/3 % − 50/3 % = 150/3 % = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Discount % in Buy X Get Y Free

Discount % = [Y ÷ (X + Y)] × 100. The total number of items taken away by the customer forms the base for discount calculation.

Profit Calculation on Actual Cost

Profit % = (Total Profit ÷ Total Actual CP) × 100. The seller's actual investment is the true Cost Price, regardless of what is claimed to the customer.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer professes to sell goods at cost price but uses a deceptive scheme or false weights, the professed cost effectively acts as the Selling Price per unit.
